Calculate Variance-Covariance Matrix for a Fitted Model Object

Source: R/vcov.R
vcov.sdid_estimate.Rd

Provides variance estimates based on the following three options

  • The bootstrap, Algorithm 2 in Arkhangelsky et al.

  • The jackknife, Algorithm 3 in Arkhangelsky et al.

  • Placebo, Algorithm 4 in Arkhangelsky et al.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'sdid_estimate'
vcov(
  object,
  method = c("bootstrap", "jackknife", "placebo"),
  replications = 200,
  num.threads = getOption("sdid.num.threads"),
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A synthdid model

method,

the CI method. The default is bootstrap (warning: this may be slow on large data sets, the jackknife option is the fastest, with the caveat that it is not recommended for SC).

replications,

the number of bootstrap replications

num.threads

The number of threads used to run replications. Defaults to getOption("sdid.num.threads"), and if that is unset, to all available hardware threads.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, reports the progress of the replications on standard error, with elapsed time and an estimate of the time left. Defaults to FALSE. In interactive sessions the report is a single line updated in place. Elsewhere it prints one line at the start and one at each further 10% of replications. Progress reporting never changes results.

...

Additional arguments (currently ignored).

Details

The jackknife is not recommended for SC, see section 5 in Arkhangelsky et al. "placebo" is the only option that works for only one treated unit.

For estimates with covariates, each replication re-estimates the coefficients on the covariates, by the estimate's covariate method. This includes the jackknife, which holds the weights fixed.

Replications run in parallel in compiled code. All resampled index sets are drawn with R's random number generator before any thread starts, so results under a given set.seed() are identical for every value of num.threads.

References

Dmitry Arkhangelsky, Susan Athey, David A. Hirshberg, Guido W. Imbens, and Stefan Wager. "Synthetic Difference in Differences". arXiv preprint arXiv:1812.09970, 2019.
